# 0015. A compiled EF Core model, regenerated by hand

**Status:** Accepted, 2026-10-22, in a change for a faster start (commit d7f47910). Recorded after the fact on
2026-11-25, from the commit, PLAN.md ("Application Architecture") and the build plan's log, as the open item from the
ADR review of 2026-11-23 asked. Its figures are the WPF app's, where it was measured.

## Context

EF Core builds its model from `OnModelCreating` the first time a context is used. Traced on the WPF app's UI thread on
2026-10-22, that build took 389 ms of the start, and the first screen's load 492 ms with it. The model is the
entities' configurations, which change only with a migration.

## Decision

- **The app runs on a compiled model** in `Infrastructure/CompiledModels/`, made by `dotnet ef dbcontext optimize
  --output-dir CompiledModels --namespace TinapayanRMS.Infrastructure.CompiledModels`. EF Core finds it through the
  generated `[assembly: DbContextModel]` attribute, so `Configure` has no `UseModel`, and the design-time commands
  (`migrations add`, `database update`) still build the model from `OnModelCreating`.
- **It's regenerated by the same command after every model change**, as a step of adding a migration, and never edited
  by hand.
- **`CompiledModelTests` fail while it's stale**: a stale model compiles and runs, since it finds properties by name, so
  the tests compare it with the configured model, its debug view (entities, properties, keys, relationships, indexes)
  and a listing of the tables, columns, store types, keys, foreign keys and indexes it maps to.

## Consequences

- The model build on the UI thread went from 389 ms to 18 ms, and the first load from 492 ms to 115 ms (the WPF app,
  2026-10-22). The MCP server and the Recipe API start on it too.
- A model change is one command more, and a test fails until it's run; an EF Core upgrade regenerates it too, as the
  move to 11.0.0 did (2026-11-21: only its version stamp and model id changed).
- Its generated files (31 on 2026-11-25) are in the repository. Coverage of Infrastructure is read without `CompiledModels/`,
  as without `Migrations/`.

## Rejected

- **The `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Tasks` build step**, which regenerates the model as part of the build: it would
  do so on every build, for a model that changes only with a migration.
- **Checking staleness with the migrations' differ**, as `has-pending-model-changes` does: it needs design-time data the
  compiled model leaves out.
- **Building the model at the start, as before**: 0.4 s of every start on the UI thread.
